items.title: Mechanistic modelling
items.summary: Process-based models (Dynamic Energy Budget theory, NicheMapR) that predict where species can live and how they interact, from physiology and microclimate.

items.title: Species interactions
items.summary: How competition between related species shifts along environmental gradients, and what lets them coexist as the climate changes.

items.title: Thermal ecology and climate change
items.summary: The microclimates animals actually experience, and what warming means for their activity, growth and survival.

items.title: Field ecology and ecophysiology
items.summary: Field measurements, environmental sensors and physiology of reptiles and amphibians, used to build models and test their predictions.
